pharm: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (S-enantiomer of citalopram)
tags: Boxed warning: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors
quick: Use only if benefit outweighs risk; neonatal effects/PPHN
Present in milk; monitor infant for sedation/poor feeding
No adjustment in mild/moderate; not studied if CrCl <20
summary: Escitalopram is an SSRI used for major depressive disorder (adults and patients 12 years and older) and generalized anxiety disorder in adults. Usual dose is 10 mg once daily, with or without food. Carries a boxed warning for increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients.
indications: Major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older

dosage.d: Initial and recommended 10 mg once daily; maximum 20 mg once daily
dosage.n: May increase to 20 mg at intervals of no less than 1 week; no greater benefit shown at 20 mg vs 10 mg

dosage.c: Major depressive disorder (pediatric 12 years and older)
dosage.d: Initial and recommended 10 mg once daily; maximum 20 mg once daily
dosage.n: May increase to 20 mg at intervals of no less than 3 weeks

dosage.d: Initial 10 mg once daily; maximum 20 mg once daily
dosage.n: May increase to 20 mg at intervals of no less than 1 week

admin: Administer orally once daily, in the morning or evening
May be given with or without food
Screen for bipolar disorder/mania before starting
When discontinuing, reduce dose gradually rather than stopping abruptly
Do not co-administer within 14 days of an MAOI
moa: Escitalopram is the S-enantiomer of racemic citalopram. Its antidepressant action is presumed to be linked to potentiation of serotonergic activity in the CNS through highly selective inhibition of neuronal reuptake of serotonin (5-HT), with minimal effect on norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake.

absolute: Concomitant use with MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI - risk of serotonin syndrome
Known hypersensitivity to escitalopram, citalopram, or any inactive ingredient
relative: History of mania/hypomania or bipolar disorder
Conditions predisposing to hyponatremia or volume depletion
monitor: Suicidal ideation and clinical worsening, especially early and after dose changes

preg: SSRI use, particularly later in pregnancy, may increase the risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN) and poor neonatal adaptation (respiratory distress, temperature instability, feeding difficulty, hypotonia, tremor, irritability). Use in the month before delivery may increase risk of postpartum hemorrhage. Available data have not established an increased risk of major birth defects or miscarriage. Weigh against risks of untreated maternal depression. A pregnancy exposure registry exists (1-844-405-6185).
lact: Escitalopram and its metabolite desmethylescitalopram are present in human milk. Reports of excessive sedation, restlessness, agitation, poor feeding, and poor weight gain in exposed infants. Consider developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: Pharmacokinetics in patients with creatinine clearance less than 20 mL/min have not been evaluated. No dosage adjustment is necessary for mild or moderate renal impairment.
hepatic: Increased exposure occurs in hepatic impairment. Recommended dosage is 10 mg once daily.

major: MAOIs (including linezolid, IV methylene blue) - contraindicated; serotonin syndrome
Other serotonergic drugs (other SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans, TCAs, opioids, lithium, buspirone, amphetamines, tryptophan, St. John's Wort) - serotonin syndrome
moderate: Drugs that interfere with hemostasis (NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin) - increased bleeding risk; monitor INR with warfarin
Drugs that prolong the QT interval - additive QT effects
CYP2D6 substrates - escitalopram may increase concentrations of such drugs
interactions.food: Absorption is not affected by food; may be taken with or without meals.
interactions.alcohol: Concomitant use with alcohol is not recommended.

emergency: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Suicidal ideation and clinical worsening, especially during initiation and dose changes
Signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome
Serum sodium in patients at risk for hyponatremia
Signs of abnormal bleeding when used with anticoagulants/antiplatelets
counsel: Watch for and report emergence of suicidal thoughts or worsening mood, especially early in treatment
Report symptoms of serotonin syndrome immediately
Do not stop abruptly; taper under medical supervision to avoid discontinuation symptoms
Inform clinician of all serotonergic drugs and St. John's Wort
May be taken with or without food
pk: Antidepressant effect over weeks; steady state in ~1 week
Store per product labeling at controlled room temperature
pearls: S-enantiomer of citalopram; metabolites contribute little to activity
Effective dose is usually 10 mg/day; 20 mg shows no clear added benefit in MDD
Bioavailability about 80%; absorption unaffected by food
Half-life increased ~50% in elderly - use 10 mg once daily
Prolonged cardiac monitoring advised in overdose due to QT/arrhythmia risk
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose may cause seizures (possibly delayed), altered mental status including coma, cardiovascular toxicity (QRS and QTc prolongation, wide-complex tachyarrhythmias, torsade de pointes), hypertension (rarely hypotension), and serotonin syndrome. Provide supportive care with prolonged cardiac monitoring; consider activated charcoal if early after ingestion. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
